Veterans and military family members are being fired by the thousands from federal jobs. Our healthcare is being gutted. Our benefits are under siege.

Now, it's our turn.

We rally to:

Defend veteran and military family member employment in the federal workforce

Stop the privatization and weakening of the Department of Veterans Affairs

Hold political leaders accountable for policies that harm veterans and their families.

title: NO KINGS! "We the People" Democracy Fair in Palo Alto
description:
This Flag Day, join us for a democracy fair. Following a day of peaceful protests held in counterpoint to Donald Trump’s militaristic charade, we will host a celebration of what makes America truly great—and truly good.

On June 14, we will gather not just in protest, but in defiance—loud, proud, joyful defiance of a tinpot wannabe tyrant who thinks that celebrating his birthday matters more than honoring the flag that symbolizes our freedom. The democracy fair will be an occasion for people to convene after No Kings events being held across the Peninsula.

It will be an active, participatory gathering that includes something for everyone: an exhibit of pro-democracy art, music and theatrical performances on the theme of “No Kings,” tables where people can learn about activism opportunities, a Resistance Lab workshop, a costume competition (Elon Musk isn’t welcome, but Elon look-alikes might get a prize), and much more.

This event—jointly sponsored by Bend the Arc, Indivisible Mid-Peninsula, Indivisible Palo Alto Plus, Indivisible Portola Valley, and It’s Blue Turn—will celebrate patriotism, not militarism. In saying NO to kings, we will also say YES to democracy.

The democracy fair will take place at Rinconada Park, and will follow a parade that starts at 2 p.m. The parade will begin at the intersection of El Camino Real and Embarcadero Road. description:
What are you doing on Flag Day? Donald Trump will be conducting a militaristic charade. We will be hosting a peaceful parade.

On June 14, we will hold a peaceful gathering that sends a bracing message to Trump and his MAGA minions: This is what an American parade looks like. No tanks, no guns, no war planes. In Washington, D.C., Trump will oversee a military display that echoes the aggressive pretensions of dictators overseas. His self-serving event will shamefully contradict the spirit of the democratic republic for which our flag stands.

In Palo Alto, as elsewhere across the country, Americans will rise up to celebrate our liberation from kingly pretension. We will gather not just in protest, but in defiance—loud, proud, joyful defiance of a tinpot wannabe tyrant who thinks that celebrating his birthday matters more than honoring the flag that symbolizes our freedom.

title: YDG University - Hate and Politics
description:
This six-week virtual course explores the historical and contemporary impact of hate groups and white nationalist militias on American politics and society. From their origins in post-Civil War America to their digital presence today, we will examine how these groups operate, recruit, and influence public discourse. Through historical case studies, data analysis, and counter-organizing strategies, students will develop a critical understanding of hate groups and the tools necessary to challenge their influence, fight misinformation, and combat hate in politics. 


By the end of this course, you will:

-Gain a comprehensive understanding of the origins and evolution of hate groups in America.

-Analyze the role of hate groups in shaping national and state politics, with a specific focus on Georgia.

-Investigate how hate groups use digital platforms to spread narratives and recruit members.

-Develop strategies to counter-organize against hate groups at both community and policy levels.

description:
Democracy isn’t a gift; it’s a responsibility. It’s the promise that every voice matters, that every life is valued. These cuts strip that promise away, leaving us divided and powerless. But we are not powerless. Together, we can demand a government that prioritizes people over profit, that restores funding to our military, workers, healthcare, and schools. Together, we can revive the democracy they’ve tried to bury.
Our military personnel, who sacrifice everything for our safety, are being abandoned. Funding for veteran services, mental health support, and active-duty resources has been slashed, leaving those who serve to fend for themselves. Workers across industries face stagnating wages and vanishing protections as labor budgets are gutted, forcing families into poverty while corporate profits soar. Medical care, a basic human right, is now a luxury—hospitals are underfunded, staff are overworked, and patients are turned away. Education, the cornerstone of an informed democracy, is crumbling; schools lack resources, teachers are underpaid, and students are left behind in overcrowded classrooms.
These cuts aren’t random. They’re a calculated move to weaken us, to silence us, to keep us too desperate to fight back. When our soldiers, workers, healthcare systems, and schools are starved, so too is our democracy. A nation that cannot care for its people is no democracy at all—it’s a hollow shell, ruled by those who profit from our suffering.
We cannot sit idly by, scrolling through outrage on screens while our country decays. Democracy dies in darkness, but it thrives in the streets, in the voices of the united, in the courage of those who show up. We must take our fight offline, where real change is forged. Join us in a nationwide protest to demand an end to these devastating cuts and a return to a government that serves its people.
The United States, once a beacon of democratic ideals, is crumbling under the weight of relentless cuts that gut the very systems we rely on—our military personnel, workers, medical care, and education. These slashes aren't just budget adjustments; they’re a deliberate attack on the backbone of our society, eroding the foundations of a free and fair nation. Democracy, as we know it, is dead—smothered in the shadows of greed, apathy, and unchecked power. But we, the people, can reignite its flame. It’s time to rise, resist, and reclaim what’s ours through unified, offline action.

title: Hope is Revolutionary: Remembering the Tulsa Massacre
description:
On May 31, 1921, white mobs burned the thriving Black community of Greenwood—known as Black Wall Street—to the ground, killing hundreds and displacing thousands. Over a century later, we gather not just to remember — but to resist.

Join Hope In Action (HIA) for a community event honoring the legacy of the Tulsa Massacre and affirming that hope is revolutionary in the face of historical and ongoing racial violence.

We remember. We organize. We give back.
We will be peacefully protesting while supporting our community through mutual aid.

We will be collecting monetary donations — all going directly to support the NAACP’s local racial justice efforts.

Let’s make memory active. Let’s turn mourning into movement.
Because remembrance without resistance is not enough.
